the project directory, and the Code, Chain, and Spec default templates end
with:

UNDERSTANDING_FILE, and keep it current as you read more of the spec. It is a
Markdown list and nothing else: one line per constraint, at most twelve, each
a single short, specific statement of what must be true, written as a link to
the spec or reference file it comes from, such as

files at the top, and "Understanding" at the bottom, with the same header
style, and how many constraints are listed, muted, at its right. The line
between them can be dragged to share the height between the two, each at
least 80 pixels tall; the split starts halfway and keeps where it was dragged
for as long as the application runs. Each half scrolls on its own with a
[ScrollbarScope](.claude/reference/ui/components/scrollbar/ScrollbarScope.md).

constraint, its text wrapping, and clicking it opens the file it links to, as

muted and does nothing when clicked. It updates as the file changes on disk,
and a row that changes or is added is briefly highlighted. Until the file

isn't a list item is left out.

# Mode System Prompts Scope

## Concept

### Pitch

The system prompt each mode sends, which tells the harness what kind of work a prompt is, and which each project can make its own.

### Shape

#### Description

Each of the [PromptModesScope](../modes/PromptModesScope.md) has a system prompt template. A prompt sent in a mode gives its hidden anchor a systemPrompt property, alongside its userPrompt, from that mode's template.

#### Templates

A template is Piton prose, like the prompt it is sent with, so it can reference the spec, with three placeholders, CODE_LOCATION, SPEC_LOCATION, and PITON_FLUENCY, each written after a dollar sign and inside braces like a Piton interpolation. Before the prompt is compiled, they are filled in: CODE_LOCATION and SPEC_LOCATION with the code location and the spec location, as the [ProjectLocationsScope](../../project-locations/ProjectLocationsScope.md) says, and PITON_FLUENCY with the project's Piton fluency. Each can be moved or removed, like any other text of the template.

#### Piton Fluency

The Piton fluency is what `piton claude --print-prompt` prints, run in the project directory. It is run once, in the background, when the project is opened, and kept for as long as the project stays open, so every prompt sent meanwhile is given the same; a prompt sent before it has finished waits for it. Where `piton` isn't installed or fails, PITON_FLUENCY is filled in with nothing, and the prompt is sent without it. A template left with nothing but blank space once filled in gives no system prompt at all. What it prints is taken as text, never read as Piton: its braces, backslashes, and interpolations reach the harness exactly as printed.

#### Saving

Each project has its own templates, saved with its data, as the [ProjectDataScope](../../project-data/ProjectDataScope.md) says, a Markdown file per mode, and edited in the [SettingsWindowScope](../../settings-window/SettingsWindowScope.md). A mode with no file yet sends its default.

#### Defaults

The defaults are the templates saved in this application's own repository, in its `.suspense/system-prompts` directory, one Markdown file per mode, named as a project's are. They are the source of truth for the defaults, and are baked into the application when it is built, so a build always ships with whatever those files say, and changing them changes the defaults the next build has. A build can't be made without them.
Every mode's default, Code, Chain, Spec, and Ask, says, after what the mode is for, on a paragraph of its own:
Links to .claude/reference/… in the prompt are the spec for what they name. Read each one before changing anything it covers.
Each then ends with PITON_FLUENCY, on a paragraph of its own.
The defaults are only where a project starts, and what resetting a template puts back. A project whose templates were saved before a default changed, such as before PITON_FLUENCY was added, keeps them as they are.

Links in this document point at reference files. Read one when the work touches what it describes.
-----

# Open File Scope

## Concept

### Pitch

Opens one of the project's files to read or edit, from wherever the file is named, always in the same place.

### Shape

#### Description

A file opens in an [EditorScope](../editor/EditorScope.md), in the split beside the chat history that the [MainWindowScope](../application/MainWindowScope.md) lays out. Opening a file while another is showing shows it in that one's place, the editor first asking to discard any unsaved changes.

#### Opened From

A file opens this way, however it is opened:

- clicking it in the [FileTreeScope](../../ui/components/file-tree/FileTreeScope.md)
- picking it in the [PaletteScope](../palette/PaletteScope.md), or its search for a file finding just that one, which closes the palette
- clicking a link to it in a task's compiled prompt or reply text, or its path on a row of the [MessageList](../prompt-mode/message-list/MessageList.md)
- the button for opening it in a [DiffViewScope](../../ui/components/diff-view/DiffViewScope.md)'s header, which closes the diff first
- going to a definition in another file from the editor, which opens that file at the definition

#### Missing

A link to a file that doesn't exist shows an error notification, and opens nothing.

Links in this document point at reference files. Read one when the work touches what it describes.

# Scrollbar Scope

## Concept

### Pitch

A permanent scrollbar for any list that scrolls, laid out as a narrow column of its own beside the list rather than over it.

### Shape

#### Description

A narrow column along the right of the list, always shown, whether or not the list has anything to scroll. It is the list's only scrollbar: no scrollbar is laid over the list, or appears only while hovering or scrolling.

#### Buttons

A square button at the top of the column scrolls the list up a little, and a square button at the bottom scrolls it down a little. The column is as wide as the buttons, with the track's line, are tall. Each button sits just inside the track, as the thumb does, never over the track's edges: the track's line runs down the column's side against the list beside it too, unbroken from the top of the column to the bottom, the button filling the width inside that line, and a pixel of the dark track lies between the button and the rest of the track, and between the down button and the lock button. The buttons draw no lines of their own; whatever holds the column draws the lines around it. The buttons have no background of their own: they are the colour of whatever the column sits on, until hovered or pressed. While the pointer is over the up or down button, it has the bevel of the [ThemeScope](../../theme/ThemeScope.md), and while it is pressed with the pointer still over it, its pressed bevel instead; neither bevel shows otherwise, and neither takes the mouse.

#### Track

#### Templates

A template is Piton prose, like the prompt it is sent with, so it can reference the spec, with four placeholders, CODE_LOCATION, SPEC_LOCATION, PITON_FLUENCY, and UNDERSTANDING_FILE, each written after a dollar sign and inside braces like a Piton interpolation. Before the prompt is compiled, the first three are filled in: CODE_LOCATION and SPEC_LOCATION with the code location and the spec location, as the [ProjectLocationsScope](../../project-locations/ProjectLocationsScope.md) says, and PITON_FLUENCY with the project's Piton fluency. Each can be moved or removed, like any other text of the template.
UNDERSTANDING_FILE stands for the path, from the project directory, of the task's understanding file, and is filled in as the prompt is sent, once the task's history record is named, so a prompt sent from the queue is given its own. A question from the Ask tab has no understanding file, and UNDERSTANDING_FILE is filled in with nothing.

#### Piton Fluency
#### Understanding File

Each Code, Chain, or Spec task has an understanding file: the short list of constraints the harness has taken from the spec for it, which the [ReferencedSpecSidebarScope](../../../ui/components/referenced-spec-sidebar/ReferencedSpecSidebarScope.md) shows as it changes. It is saved beside the task's history record, with the same name and the extension `.understanding.md`, written by the harness itself. Nothing else writes it, and nothing is there until the harness writes it.

#### Defaults

The defaults are the templates saved in this application's own repository, in its `.suspense/system-prompts` directory, one Markdown file per mode, named as a project's are. They are the source of truth for the defaults, and are baked into the application when it is built, so a build always ships with whatever those files say, and changing them changes the defaults the next build has. A build can't be made without them.
Every mode's default, Code, Chain, Spec, and Ask, says, after what the mode is for, on a paragraph of its own:
Links to .claude/reference/… in the prompt are the spec for what they name. Read each one before changing anything it covers.
Each then has PITON_FLUENCY, on a paragraph of its own. Ask's ends there. The Code, Chain, and Spec defaults then end with, on a paragraph of its own:
"Before changing anything, write the constraints this task must meet to ${UNDERSTANDING_FILE}, and keep it current as you read more of the spec. It is a Markdown list and nothing else: one line per constraint, at most twelve, each a single short, specific statement of what must be true, written as a link to the spec or reference file it comes from, such as `- [The chain tab has no bottom border in combined mode](spec/scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.pi)`. Only list what the spec says; leave out anything you are deciding yourself. Replace a constraint when you learn it was wrong rather than adding another."
The defaults are only where a project starts, and what resetting a template puts back. A project whose templates were saved before a default changed, such as before PITON_FLUENCY was added, keeps them as they are.

Links in this document point at reference files. Read one when the work touches what it describes.
